population.span: consecutive adult patients admitted for elective cardiac surgeries randomly received a 1-mg dose of colchicine (n = 81) or placebo (n = 71) orally 12 to 24 hours before surgery followed by a daily dose of 0.5 mg until hospital discharge.

endpoint.span: The primary efficacy endpoint was the development of at least one episode of AF (lasting 5 minutes or longer) occurring after cardiac surgery at any point during hospitalization.

estimate.span: Comparing the colchicine and placebo groups, the odds ratio was 0.85 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.37–1.99).

ci.span: Comparing the colchicine and placebo groups, the odds ratio was 0.85 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.37–1.99).

analysis_set.span: Among the 152 randomized patients, AF occurred in 26 patients (17%), including 16% of patients in the colchicine group and 18.3% of patients in the placebo group.

treatment_strategy.span: Upon enrollment, patients were treated with 1 mg of colchicine or matching placebo 12 to 24 hours prior to surgery, followed by colchicine (0.5 mg) or placebo immediately after their surgery (via a nasogastric tube) and daily treatment at this dose until hospital discharge.

follow_up.span: occurring after cardiac surgery at any point during hospitalization.

served_mismatch: The served outcome requests RR, whereas the directly reported estimate and confidence interval are OR 0.85 (95% CI 0.37–1.99). The served arm-level event counts agree with the source; no numeric RR or RR confidence interval is supplied in served_row to compare. The source describes outcomes among the 152 randomized patients but does not explicitly label the analysis intention-to-treat.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The randomized entry population consists of adults admitted for elective cardiac surgery, within the question's population.
entry_population_matches_question.span: consecutive adult patients admitted for elective cardiac surgeries randomly received a 1-mg dose of colchicine (n = 81) or placebo (n = 71) orally 12 to 24 hours before surgery followed by a daily dose of 0.5 mg until hospital discharge.

notes: All spans use the held full text. The bound estimate is the reported OR for overall in-hospital POAF; no RR or RR confidence interval was calculated. The analysis-set span reports outcomes among all 152 randomized patients without a formal ITT designation.
